core.title: Drive flow router tests through the production runners, not mocks
core.given: An end-to-end test that exercises a flow router route or user/system flow
core.when: the test is written or changed to prove route/user-system-flow behavior
core.then: Drive the production runner chain — the route-resolution runner that resolves the guarded route to exactly one selected user/system flow, then the user/system-flow-execution runner that executes it — so the asserted evidence comes from the real runners, with no mock, substituted runner or hand-built resolver standing in for them.
prefer: Invoke the production route-resolution runner, constructed over the flow router plan artifact, with guard-relevant inputs; it resolves the guarded route to exactly one selected user/system flow.
Pass that selected user/system flow to the production user/system-flow-execution runner and execute it through the real execution path.
Assert the selected user/system flow and the route- or acceptance-specific result of its execution.
avoid: Mock objects standing in for either production runner (a mock route-resolution or user/system-flow-execution runner).
The test framework's module-mocking idiom applied to a runner module (worst case: it swaps the entire route-control module).

Spy, stub or restore idioms of the current test framework aimed at a runner; mock idioms of a framework the suite is migrating from applied around a runner module; spy idioms of a migrating framework that replace a runner's route-resolution/execution behavior (a migrating-framework spy that only observes, without replacing behavior, is not itself forbidden).
A hand-built route resolver (a local route-resolution function or resolver class) standing in for the production route-resolution runner.
Importing the real runners only to satisfy the check while assertions come from a parallel fake path.
Asserting a plan literal without driving production route resolution and execution.
unless: Not a flow router test: no flow router route/user-system-flow token and no production runner symbol.
core.why: A test that replaces either runner with a double exercises the double, not production route control — a descriptive green proving nothing about production.
evidence: The test references both production runners (route resolution and user/system flow execution) and contains none of the forbidden substitution patterns.
Breaking production route-resolution or user/system-flow-execution behavior would make the test red.
The asserted evidence (selected user/system flow and its execution result) comes from the real runner chain.
verification: Strict disposition: a finding of this rule blocks (severity 1).

Scope: the check scans the stack's end-to-end tests (roles.e2e_test.path) that are interlocking-related — a test is interlocking-related if it references any flow router route/user-system-flow token or a production runner symbol; otherwise it is out of scope.
Check 1: a flow router test must reference BOTH production runners — the route-resolution runner and the user/system-flow-execution runner (roles.runtime_components#flow_router_runner).

Check 2: any one forbidden substitution pattern — a test double replacing a production runner, enumerated by the stack's own idioms (idiom.test_constructs#forbidden_runner_substitutions) — is a violation.
Comments are masked before pattern matching, so a forbidden pattern that appears only inside a comment is not a violation.

Symbol reference is only a structural proxy, not sufficient semantic proof: a reviewer must confirm that the case drives the production runners with guard-relevant inputs and observes the claimed route/user-system-flow behavior.

The production runner chain is the flow router call model (design ref afokapu/atdd#1251): entry -> route resolution (guarded route to exactly one selected user/system flow) -> user/system flow execution.
Discovery scope, the comment-masking mechanics and the exact pattern list are delegated to the stack realization.

fires: An end-to-end test references a flow router route but never references the user/system-flow-execution runner.
A flow router end-to-end test replaces a runner module with the test framework's module-mocking idiom.
A flow router end-to-end test defines a hand-built route resolver (a local route-resolution function or resolver class) instead of driving the production route-resolution runner.
A flow router end-to-end test uses the current test framework's spy/mock/restore idiom aimed at a runner.
A flow router end-to-end test uses a migrating framework's spy idiom to replace runner behavior (route resolution / user/system flow execution).
doesNotFire: An end-to-end test with no flow router route/user-system-flow token and no production runner symbol.
A forbidden pattern that appears only inside a comment (comments are masked).
Flow router tests realized in another stack, which owns its own rendering of this rule.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the stack's end-to-end tests live; this is the discovery scope of the rule's check.

The stack's concrete symbols, entry points and full invocation shape for the two production flow router runners — the route-resolution runner (constructed over the flow router plan artifact, invoked with an action and inputs, resolving the guarded route to exactly one selected user/system flow) and the user/system-flow-execution runner (which receives that selected user/system flow and executes it through the real runtime path) — which a flow router test must reference and drive, including the selected-user/system-flow handoff between the two runners.
profileRequirements.bunValue: FlowRouterRunner and FlowRunner; call model FlowRouterRunner.resolveUserSystemFlow -> FlowRunner.execute; construct new FlowRouterRunner(flowRouterYamlPath) and call .resolveUserSystemFlow(action, inputs), which resolves the guarded route to exactly one userSystemFlowId; pass that userSystemFlowId to the production FlowRunner and execute the selected user/system flow through the real runtime path

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's test-double idioms that count as a forbidden substitution when aimed at a production runner or its route-resolution/execution behavior, including mock classes and hand-built resolvers standing in for the route-resolution runner; a migrating-framework spy idiom counts only when it replaces runner behavior.
profileRequirements.bunValue: MockFlowRouterRunner/MockFlowRunner; mock.module(...) replacing a runner module; spyOn(...)/mock(...)/mock.restore(...) aimed at a runner (bun:test); vi.mock(...)/jest.mock(...) around a runner module; vi.spyOn(...)/jest.spyOn(...) replacing runner behavior (resolveUserSystemFlow/execute); a locally defined resolveUserSystemFlow function or *Resolver class standing in for FlowRouterRunner

bunOnly.reason: Finding and detector ids of this one rule are realization details; the core's verification names the two failure modes generically (missing production-runner reference; forbidden substitution pattern).

bunOnly.text: JS detector, member of the bun_flow_router_coverage family; scans the consumer's interlocking-related e2e/**/*.ts tests with comments masked.
bunOnly.reason: Detector identity, implementation language and family id are Bun-realization details; the neutral scope (interlocking-related end-to-end tests, comments masked) is kept in core:verification.

neutralityNotes: The domain vocabulary 'flow router', 'route', 'user/system flow', 'guarded route' and the two-runner call model (afokapu/atdd#1251) are stack-neutral concepts of the ATDD framework itself (they appear in the rule id), so they stay in the core. What could not be made neutral: (1) the concrete runner symbols, entry points and invocation shape — constructor over the flow router plan artifact, the (action, inputs) call resolving to exactly one selected user/system flow, and the selected-user/system-flow handoff to the execution runner — carried as the proposed profile key roles.runtime_components#flow_router_runner so each stack supplies its own; (2) the enumerated forbidden substitution idioms (mock.module, bun:test spyOn/mock/mock.restore, vi.mock/jest.mock, vi.spyOn/jest.spyOn only when replacing runner behavior, local resolveUserSystemFlow/*Resolver) — carried as the proposed profile key idiom.test_constructs#forbidden_runner_substitutions; (3) the discovery glob e2e/**/*.ts — carried as roles.e2e_test.path; (4) the language fact (typescript/bun) and the detector/family/finding ids (bun_flow_router_coverage, missing_production_runner_symbol, forbidden_substitution) — bunOnly, per the notProfileKeys rule. Masking is comment-only, exactly as the Bun rewrite specifies; the mechanics of masking are delegated to the stack realization.
